coverage_note: Employees of counties, cities and other political subdivisions (and the other groups the chapter names) under the Public Employees' Collective Bargaining Act, RCW chapter 41.56, administered by the Public Employment Relations Commission. State civil service employees (RCW 41.80), teachers and other certificated school employees (RCW 41.59) and higher-education groups have separate or additional provisions not covered cell by cell here. The chapter was recodified by 2025 c 290; pinpoints use the current section numbers.

governing_statute.value: Public Employees' Collective Bargaining Act, RCW chapter 41.56
governing_statute.quote: The intent and purpose of this chapter is to promote the continued improvement of the relationship between public employers and their employees by providing a uniform basis for implementing the right of public employees to join labor organizations of their own choosing

ulp_limitation_period.value: Six months before the filing of the complaint with PERC (or in superior court)
ulp_limitation_period.quote: That a complaint shall not be processed for any unfair labor practice occurring more than six months before the filing of the complaint with the commission or in superior court.

who_may_bargain.value: Employees of counties, municipal corporations and other political subdivisions, including district and superior courts, excluding elected officials, fixed-term board and commission appointees, confidential employees and others listed in the definition; the chapter also reaches specified state-paid provider groups and others
who_may_bargain.quote: This chapter shall apply to any county or municipal corporation, or any political subdivision of the state of Washington, including district courts and superior courts, except as otherwise provided by RCW 54.04.170 , 54.04.180 , and chapters 41.59 , 47.64, and 53.18 RCW.

scope_of_bargaining.value: Grievance procedures and personnel matters including wages, hours and working conditions; matters delegated to a qualifying civil service commission need not be bargained
scope_of_bargaining.quote: to execute a written agreement with respect to grievance procedures, subject to RCW 41.58.070 , and collective negotiations on personnel matters, including wages, hours, and working conditions, which may be peculiar to an appropriate bargaining unit of such public employer

impasse_procedure.value: Either party may submit any matter in dispute to PERC (mediation) when no agreement is reached; uniformed personnel (police, fire and similar) go on to binding interest arbitration under RCW 41.56.501 to 41.56.540
impasse_procedure.quote: (2) Upon the failure of the public employer and the exclusive bargaining representative to conclude a collective bargaining agreement, any matter in dispute may be submitted by either party to the commission.

strike_legality.value: Not granted by the chapter; uniformed personnel strikes are expressly prohibited (RCW 41.56.545)
strike_legality.quote: Nothing contained in this chapter shall permit or grant any public employee the right to strike or refuse to perform his or her official duties.

agency_fee_status.value: Not enforceable against nonconsenting public employees after Janus v. AFSCME Council 31 (2018); dues deduction rests on employee authorization (RCW 41.56.061)
agency_fee_status.quote: For these reasons, States and public-sector unions may no longer extract agency fees from nonconsenting employees.

dfr_forum.value: PERC, through an unfair labor practice complaint against the bargaining representative; the statute does not name a duty of fair representation, and PERC's treatment of such claims rests on decisions not captured
dfr_forum.quote: It shall be an unfair labor practice for a bargaining representative: (1) To interfere with, restrain, or coerce public employees in the exercise of their rights guaranteed by this chapter;
